children: Auto stocks came under sharp selling pressure in early trade on September 2, with the Nifty Auto index falling more than 2 percent despite broadly strong August sales reported by automakers and positive demand commentary from brokerages.

The Nifty Auto was down 2.03 percent at 27,912.35 around 9:23 am, making it one of the top sectoral losers. The decline was steeper than the broader market, with the Nifty 50 down 1.05 percent at 23,803.10 and the Sensex falling 755 points to 76,188.87.

All the Nifty Auto constituents were trading in the red. Eicher Motors was the biggest loser, falling 2.8 percent to Rs 7,747, followed by Tube Investments of India and Samvardhana Motherson, which declined 2.67 percent and 2.62 percent, respectively.
Sona BLW Precision Forgings fell 2.57 percent, Bosch dropped 2.41 percent, Hero MotoCorp lost 2.32 percent to Rs 5,426 and Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) declined 2.26 percent to Rs 3,185.30.

Ashok Leyland was down 2.07 percent at Rs 167, while TVS Motor fell 1.56 percent to Rs 4,137.60. Maruti Suzuki declined 1.31 percent to Rs 12,780, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles slipped 1.24 percent to Rs 306.15 and Bajaj Auto was down 1.17 percent at Rs 12,216.
Automobiles' demand remains robust in August

The broad-based weakness came despite a robust set of August sales numbers across much of the automobile industry. Indian automakers’ sales rose strongly from a year earlier, helped by healthy demand as well as a favourable base from August 2025, when customers had deferred purchases ahead of tax cuts.

Jefferies said auto demand remained strong in August, with registrations of two-wheelers, passenger vehicles and trucks growing 24-29 percent year-on-year. Tractor registrations were relatively weak, rising just 3 percent.

The brokerage estimated domestic wholesale growth of 36-43 percent for passenger vehicles and trucks and around 10 percent for two-wheelers and tractors. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles was the standout with 56 percent year-on-year growth, while Ashok Leyland, M&M, Bajaj Auto, Maruti Suzuki and TVS Motor recorded growth of 21-38 percent.
CV sales top expectations; supply constraints drag Maruti, Hyundai

Nomura also highlighted strong demand, particularly in medium and heavy commercial vehicles. It said Tata Motors CV and Bajaj Auto significantly exceeded expectations, while weaker numbers at Maruti, Hyundai and TVS Motor reflected supply constraints rather than weak demand. Nomura's preferred picks in the sector are M&M, Hyundai Motor India, Tata Motors CV, TVS Motor and Sona Comstar.

Bajaj Auto had reported a 28 percent jump in August sales to 5.35 lakh units, comfortably beating Nomura's estimate of 4.88 lakh units. M&M's overall sales rose 42 percent to 1.07 lakh units. Both stocks had gained in the previous session following the numbers.

Commercial vehicles were another bright spot. Tata Motors CV reported a 49 percent year-on-year increase in sales to 44,411 units, ahead of Nomura's estimate of 38,800 units, while Ashok Leyland's sales jumped 38 percent to 21,038 units, also beating estimates.

Citi said August volumes were strong across most original equipment manufacturers, though the year-on-year numbers benefited from the weak base following last year's GST cut. The brokerage highlighted particularly impressive commercial vehicle demand at Ashok Leyland and Tata Motors CV despite a less favourable base effect. Its preference in the sector is Maruti Suzuki, followed by Eicher Motors and M&M.

title: Nifty Auto falls 2% despite strong August sales; Eicher, M&M, Hero MotoCorp lead losses
